Sequential prefix-year-counter numbers exist for ordinary documents; Special Report display codes omit schedule identity and can repeat.
Select document type, category, and subcategory.
Document and communication types and transaction classification exist; no category/subcategory taxonomy.
Record reference number and reference date.
Reference number exists; no dedicated reference-date field.
Record the source and method of receipt: physical, email, courier, or digital.
Source and communication type exist; receipt channel is not a separate configurable field.
Flag confidential, urgent, or restricted documents.
Normal/Urgent priority exists; no confidentiality or restricted-access classification.
Draft registration that can be completed later.
A valid received record can be saved without forwarding; there is no incomplete draft/autosave state.
Record linking for related documents, attachments, and previous submissions.
External document URLs exist; no related-record links or previous-submission relationship model.
Unique tracking number for every document.
Ordinary documents have sequential DTS codes; Special Reports generated by different schedules can share SR-year-month labels.
Total processing time from receipt to closure.
Elapsed/current-stage and working-day turnaround are available; the principal turnaround KPI starts at assignment and stops at clearance, not receipt-to-final-release.
Reason for return, rejection, cancellation, or reassignment.
Return reasons are required and reassignment notes are supported; cancellation/rejection states and universally mandatory reassignment reasons are absent.
Archived, closed, cancelled, and reopened records.
Released records remain searchable; no archive/cancel/reopen lifecycle.
Viewable movement receipt for every handoff.
Printable routing slip contains movements; there is no separate acknowledged receipt per handoff.
Forward documents between offices and employees.
The defined Admin-to-Focal-to-Staff/reviewer chain works; unrestricted office-to-office routing is absent.
Send documents to multiple reviewers when necessary.
Several reviewers act sequentially; no selected multi-reviewer task set.
Require sequential reviews or allow parallel reviews.
Sequential reviews exist; parallel reviews do not.
The live hierarchy exists, but arbitrary hierarchies are not configurable through the designer.
Delegate work during leave or official travel.
Manager presence/OIC can be set manually; personnel leave does not automatically trigger delegation.
Configure routing by document type, source, urgency, or amount/category.
Reporting-period documents route through configured region/office designations; arbitrary source/urgency/amount rules exist only as designer simulation, if supported there.
Require a reason when rejecting, cancelling, or bypassing a step.
Return-to-sender/correction reasons are required; bypass clear can lack a required reason, and cancel/reject actions do not exist.
Configure exceptional routing with proper authorization.
Override/OIC and reporting designations exist; generic executable exception-rule configuration is absent.
Preserve the original assignee and full routing history after reassignment.
History names the original and replacement assignees; a dedicated immutable original-assignee ID is not maintained.
Provide a workflow preview showing the next responsible person.
Current-desk/lifecycle information and designer simulation show candidates; there is no fully integrated preview of all next operational tasks.
assignedBy is stored/displayed; no dedicated Assigned by me view or filter.
Task priority: low, normal, high, urgent.
Normal/Urgent exists; Low/High levels are absent.
Remarks, review instructions and notes exist; no structured deliverable/task specification.
Due date and expected completion date.
Calculated due date exists; no independent estimated completion date.
Reassignment accepts a note but does not require a reason in every case.
Attach the resulting document or output.
Draft/revised URLs can reference output files; direct output upload is absent.
Record time spent on a task, if required.
Elapsed stage time exists; no actual effort/timesheet entry.
Reminders for tasks approaching their deadline.
Due-soon badges and a queue bell are visible; no scheduled reminder delivery.
Configure separate deadlines for each workflow stage.
Admin/Focal desk limits exist; no independently configured processing/review/approval SLA for every stage.
Due-soon display threshold is configurable; repeating notification intervals are absent.
Desk counts, age bands and stalled records help manual analysis; no historical per-stage bottleneck diagnosis.
Track repeated overdue cases by office, document type, or assigned person.
Current overdue workload is grouped/filterable; no dedicated repeated-overdue case history metric.
Upload working drafts and final outputs.
Working/revised external file URLs exist; files are not uploaded into DTS.
Current draft/revised links are explicit; no version list or latest/final version state.
Record who uploaded or revised each version.
URL edits have actor/time events; no uploader or per-version file record.
Revision counter and URL-change events exist; old file links, version descriptions and version metadata are not retained.
Resubmission resolves all outstanding review comments together; no individual comment-resolution control.
Preview PDFs and common office documents where supported.
External URL hover attempts an iframe preview; CSP restricts external frames and there is no native PDF/Office renderer.
Link related memoranda, reports, letters, and references.
External URLs can point to references; no related-record relationship or multi-reference list.
Record review, endorsement, approval, and signature dates separately.
Review and clearance dates exist; endorsement and actual signature dates are not separate fields.
Attach signed copies and proof of completion.
A URL can point to a signed/output file; no dedicated signed-copy or proof-of-completion attachment slot.
Generate transmittal sheets and routing slips.
Routing slips are printable; no separate numbered transmittal sheet generator.
Identify incomplete submissions before sending them for approval.
Form/action validation covers required metadata and reviewer selection; no attachment/deliverable completeness gate.
Normal/Urgent classification exists; broader priority levels are absent.
Existing DTS tracking number remains on release; no separate outgoing control/transmittal numbering.
Clearance and dispatch times exist; actual signature date is absent.
Review forwarding and notes can represent endorsement; no endorsement action/status.
Division/focal/staff routing exists; arbitrary interoffice handoff/receipt tracking is absent.
Document/communication/transaction types exist; no formal records classification/retention taxonomy.
Released records remain searchable; no archive repository/lifecycle.
Document deletion is authorized/audited; no retention-based disposal authorization/log model.
Separate incoming and outgoing registries with cross-references.
Incoming/outgoing subsets share one record; no separate linked registry records.
Record returned or undelivered outgoing correspondence.
Return-to-sender before release exists; no post-dispatch undelivered/returned-delivery state.
Permissions at module, record, and action levels.
Module/action/stage and division action gates exist; record viewing is universal for signed-in users.
Separate permission to view, edit, assign, approve, export, and delete.
Edit/assign/review/export/delete permissions exist; no independent document-view permission.
OIC or alternate-officer delegation with start and end dates.
OIC enablement and manager presence exist; no start/end-dated delegation.
Session expiration and optional multi-factor authentication.
Idle/absolute session expiration exists; optional MFA is absent.
Prevention of self-approval where policy requires separation of duties.
Submission prevents selecting oneself as reviewer; there is no universal separation-of-duties rule across manager/override actions.
Department review/clearance queues exist; signature itself is not separately tracked.
Documents with no activity for a configurable period.
Admin/Focal desk age limits exist; no universal last-activity inactivity threshold across all stages.
Current desks and age bands are visible; no historical stage-duration bottleneck analysis.
History updates and recent-action flashes exist; no dedicated recent-updates feed/widget.
Released status and received-date reporting exist; no archive view or dedicated recently-completed widget.
Entering a tracking code finds matches through substring search; no exact-match-only search mode.
Search by sender, recipient, subject, reference number, or office.
Sender/subject/reference/office are searchable; outgoing recipient is not included in the search haystack.
Search by assigned staff, focal person, or division.
Assignee/division/current desk users are searchable; no dedicated focal-person filter.
Search by date received, date assigned, deadline, or date completed.
Received dates, release-from date and deadline states exist; assigned-date and exact completion/deadline range filters are incomplete.
Filter by status, priority, document type, confidentiality, and source.
Status/priority/type/communication filters exist; confidentiality and structured source-channel filters are absent.
Filter by overdue, approaching deadline, or no recent activity.
Overdue/due-soon and stalled desk filters exist; general no-recent-activity filtering is absent.
Sort by deadline, age, date received, or last activity.
Due date, received date and current-stage age sort exist; no stored last-modified sort field.
The bell opens current actionable documents; it is not a persistent event notification center.
Badge counts waiting documents, not unread notifications.
Assignments appear in the queue/bell after refresh; no event-specific notification record.
Notifications when a document is forwarded.
Forwarded documents appear for the next actor; no persistent forwarding alert.
Notifications when a reviewer returns a document.
Returned documents appear for staff action; no persistent return alert.
Notifications when a document is approved.
Approved work appears at the next desk; no persistent approval alert.
Visible overdue badges/counts exist; no escalation alerts/delivery.
Released registry subset exists; fixed CSV omits outgoing recipient and release remarks required for a richer outgoing register.
Compliance filter and per-document cycles/comments exist; no dedicated consolidated revision report.
Stalled Admin/Focal records are available; arbitrary inactivity reporting is absent.
Daily, weekly, and monthly accomplishment reports.
Date-range reports and monthly graphs exist; no dedicated action-date accomplishment summary template.
Average turnaround and current desk ages exist; no complete historical stage bottleneck report.
Reassignment/delegation audit events can be searched; no dedicated report.
Received versus completed documents by month.
Monthly charts exist, but records are first filtered by received month, which can omit old-backlog documents released in the selected month.
Average, median, and maximum processing time.
Average turnaround exists; median/maximum turnaround are absent from app reports.
Average compliance cycles for finished documents exist; no explicit returned-document percentage.
Volume by source, document type, and division.
Type/division volumes exist; source grouping is not supplied as a report.
Drill-down from charts to the underlying document records.
Many graph bars/desk counts open registry filters; age-band drill-down drops its specific age selection (see warning).
Exportable report data with filters and a report generation timestamp.
Filtered CSV exists and print headers contain timestamp; CSV does not consistently carry generation metadata.
Filter by division, document type, status, employee, and urgency.
Registry supports these filters; Analytics/Reports offer narrower filters and exports differ by screen.
Fixed report groups and registry sorting exist; arbitrary grouping/report layout configuration is absent.
Recurring Special Report work items are generated; scheduled exports of operational reports are absent.
Include generated-by, generated-on, and reporting-period information.
Print header includes user/time/period; CSV metadata is inconsistent.
Apply permissions to exported data, not just the on-screen view.
Data comes through authenticated state, but export/print restrictions are often browser UI gates; no server-side export endpoint checks or confidential-row filtering.

Empty URLs can be seen in the form; no broken-link/missing-required-file validator.

Record downloads or exports of sensitive documents where appropriate.
System backup export is audited; ordinary file opening/download and report CSV exports are not logged.
Record who viewed, edited, assigned, forwarded, returned, approved, or closed it, where appropriate.
Successful mutations/actions are logged; document views are not individually logged.
Store previous and new values for important metadata changes.
Some Special Report configuration differences record old/new values; ordinary metadata edits only record a generic Details edited event.
Record the reason for reassignment, cancellation, or exceptional routing.
Return instructions/optional reassignment notes exist; not every exception requires a reason and cancellation is absent.
Record changes to deadlines and workflow configuration.
Configuration/workflow events are audited; no complete per-document old/new deadline ledger or pause/extension reasons.
Record document and attachment deletion attempts.
Successful document deletes are audited; denied deletion attempts and attachment deletion are not comprehensively recorded.
Action/stage authorization exists; confidential/division record-view authorization does not.
Protection against SQL injection, cross-site scripting, and cross-site request forgery where applicable.
Prepared SQL, HTML escaping, CSP and custom-header CSRF checks exist; CSV formula safety and broader attack coverage still need work.
Input validation on both client and server.
Validation exists, but restore nested data and some action-field consistency are incomplete.
Rate limiting and login attempt controls.
Failed-login throttling exists; no general API/IP rate limiter and login keys are held in memory.
Protection against unauthorized direct file access.
Static serving uses an explicit allowlist; external file access is controlled by the external host, not DTS.
No third-party app dependencies; no automated Node/container/browser vulnerability/update process is provided.
JSON round-trip tests exist; automated daily SQLite snapshot verification is absent and malformed restore can persist invalid state.
JSON database restore exists; no attachment recovery or complete disaster-recovery procedure.
Retention is hard-coded to fourteen files; no setting.
healthz checks server response; no disk-space/storage monitoring.
Database connection and application error logs.
Server writes console errors; no durable structured log/diagnostic viewer.
Special Report schedule generation issues are stored/shown; no generalized failed-job or notification monitor.
Backup export/restore audit events exist; normal report/file exports and general imports lack a history model.
Configurable document types, priorities, and statuses.
Types are configurable; priority set and operational statuses are fixed.
Holidays are configurable; working weekdays are fixed to Monday-Friday.
Prefix is configurable; year/counter structure is fixed.
package.json version and engineering notes exist; no user-facing deployment/update history.
JSON backups include settings; recovery still has the validation defect.
Mandatory/relationship validation exists in selected endpoints; no incoming document duplicate detector and restore validation is incomplete.
Import history and rollback where feasible.
Backup restore is audited and SQL writes use a transaction; no general import rollback/history tool, and post-commit load can fail.
Migration utilities from the existing DTS.
Automatic compatibility upgrades and JSON restore exist; no cross-system migration/import wizard.
Selected checks/tests exist; no explicit post-migration integrity validation report.
A back-to-dashboard link exists; no hierarchical breadcrumb trail.
Resizable columns and configurable column visibility.
Column visibility is saved; draggable/resizable column widths are absent.
Filters/sort survive within UI session; named/persisted filter and sort presets are absent.
Confirmation for destructive or irreversible actions.
Delete/restore/batch actions confirm; some consequential individual transitions do not universally confirm.
Workflow designer warns on unsaved changes; ordinary document forms lack a general dirty-form warning/autosave.
Shared formatters exist; client uses its local timezone while server defaults to Asia/Manila, so cross-timezone consistency is not guaranteed.
Accessible color contrast and keyboard navigation.
Labels, native controls and shortcuts exist; no comprehensive contrast/keyboard accessibility audit was supplied.
Agency image assets and configurable organization name exist; logo replacement is a file edit, not an upload setting.
Automatically assign documents based on document type or originating office.
Configured reporting-period document types route by region/office designation; arbitrary rule-based auto-assignment is absent.
Ordinary tracking numbers are generated automatically; Special Report display-number uniqueness needs correction.
Automatically notify the next responsible person after forwarding.
The next actor's queue/bell updates; no persistent event notification or delivery.
Routing slips are generated on demand; no automatic transmittal numbering/sheet job.
Automatically remind users about documents awaiting their action.
Queue and due-soon indicators exist; no active scheduled reminders.
Automatically flag unusual inactivity or repeated returns.
Admin/Focal stalled thresholds and revision cycle counts exist; no generalized inactivity/repeated-return anomaly rules.
Provide configurable rules for exceptional situations.
OIC/override/resubmission/reference rules exist; designer conditions do not execute production workflows.
Internal discussion threads attached to documents.
Timestamped notes and reviewer comments exist; no nested threaded discussions.
Private internal notes separated from official correspondence.
Notes are separate from the external file, but have no private visibility tier.
Staff/workload views share document action lists; no independent shared task-list objects.
Manager present/away flags and personnel leave calendar exist; staff leave is not automatically integrated into routing availability.
Delegation during leave or official travel.
Manual manager/OIC delegation exists; no general timed staff substitution linked to leave.
Handover notes when an employee leaves or changes assignment.
Reassignment accepts a note; no structured employee departure/handover record.
Activity feed showing recent team actions.
Authorized audit/history can show actions; no separate recent team activity feed.
Google Drive links or API integration.
Drive URLs can be stored; no authenticated Drive API integration.
Calendar integration for deadlines and reminders.
Personnel calendar is implemented; document-deadline calendar/sync/reminders are absent.
Internal API for future agency systems.
Internal cookie-authenticated APIs exist; no published service API/auth contract for other agency systems.
Export to existing departmental reporting templates.
Generic reports/routing slips exist; no agency template import/mapping/export integration.
Workload, desk-age and return-cycle indicators exist; no historical process mining or automatic workload balancing.
Simple Admin/Focal stall thresholds exist; no statistical/anomaly model.
Indexed database columns for common searches.
IDs and workflow/report lookup indexes exist; ordinary searchable document metadata is JSON and is searched in browser memory.
Graph/report/restore operations use SQL transactions; ordinary document mutation, sequence and audit writes are not one combined transaction.
Prevention of duplicate submissions and conflicting updates.
Workflow drafts have revision conflict checks and recurring reports have unique keys; ordinary updates lack general revision/idempotency protection and user creation has a confirmed race.
Workflow foreign keys and recurring-report uniqueness exist; many user/document/division references inside JSON have no database constraints.
Background jobs for scheduled reports and bulk processing.
In-process timers generate recurring reports; no durable worker queue or bulk-processing job system.
Console error logging exists; no centralized persistent error service/view.
CREATE IF NOT EXISTS and compatibility upgrades exist; no numbered migration ledger.
Concurrent requests are tested; independent simultaneous user-session soak testing is absent.
JSON restore round trips are tested; full snapshot disaster recovery and malformed restore rejection are incomplete.
Separation of development, testing, and production environments.
DATA_DIR and isolated test runner separate databases; no formal development/staging/production deployment configuration.
